summary: Alpelisib is an oral, selective inhibitor of the alpha isoform of phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K). As PIQRAY it is used with fulvestrant to treat adults with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has progressed on an endocrine regimen, at a dose of 300 mg (two 150 mg tablets) once daily with food. As VIJOICE it is approved (accelerated approval) for severe PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS) in patients 2 years and older. Its major hazards are severe hyperglycemia (sometimes with hyperosmolar non-ketotic syndrome or ketoacidosis) and severe cutaneous adverse reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme, toxic epidermal necrolysis and DRESS; it can also cause severe hypersensitivity, pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease, and severe diarrhea or colitis. Fasting glucose and HbA1c must be checked and optimized before and during therapy.
indications: In combination with fulvestrant for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer after progression on an endocrine-based regimen (PIQRAY)
Severe manifestations of PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS) requiring systemic therapy in patients 2 years and older (VIJOICE, accelerated approval)

Take at approximately the same time each day
For patients who cannot swallow tablets, prepare a suspension/mixture per labeling (VIJOICE granules or tablets in water)

If a PIQRAY dose is missed it can be taken with food within 9 hours of the usual time; after more than 9 hours skip that day
moa: Alpelisib is an inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) with inhibitory activity predominantly against the alpha catalytic isoform (PI3K-alpha, encoded by PIK3CA). Activating (gain-of-function) PIK3CA mutations drive constitutive PI3K-alpha and downstream Akt signalling, promoting cellular transformation, tumor growth, and the overgrowths/malformations of PROS. By inhibiting PI3K-alpha, alpelisib reduces phosphorylation of downstream targets including Akt. In hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, PI3K inhibition increases estrogen-receptor transcription, providing the rationale for combination with fulvestrant, with which it shows greater antitumor activity than either agent alone in PIK3CA-mutant models.

absolute: Severe hypersensitivity to alpelisib or any of its ingredients
relative: Type 1 diabetes or uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (safety not established)
History of severe cutaneous adverse reactions

preg: Based on animal data and its mechanism of action, alpelisib can cause fetal harm. In rats and rabbits it caused embryofetal mortality, reduced fetal weight and fetal malformations. Advise pregnant women of the risk to the fetus; women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for a period after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on alpelisib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or on milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for one week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for patients with mild to moderate renal impairment. The pharmacokinetics in severe renal impairment have not been adequately studied.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Use in severe hepatic impairment has not been established.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - may markedly decrease alpelisib levels and efficacy; avoid
Breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitors - may increase alpelisib exposure and toxicity; avoid
moderate: Antidiabetic drugs - may need dose adjustment because alpelisib causes hyperglycemia
Other QT-affecting or hyperglycemia-inducing drugs - additive metabolic effects
interactions.food: Take with food; food increases and standardizes alpelisib absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; it may aggravate hyperglycemia and gastrointestinal effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c; alpelisib commonly raises blood glucose.

common: Nausea, decreased appetite, fatigue, weight loss
serious: Severe hyperglycemia, including hyperglycemic hyperosmolar non-ketotic syndrome and ketoacidosis
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS)
Severe diarrhea or colitis with dehydration and acute kidney injury
rare: Acute kidney injury secondary to severe diarrhea/dehydration
emergency: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS

monitoring: Fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c at baseline and periodically; self-monitor glucose during treatment
Skin examination for rash and severe cutaneous reactions
Respiratory symptoms and imaging if pneumonitis suspected
Bowel pattern for diarrhea and colitis (abdominal pain, blood/mucus in stool)
Renal function and hydration status during diarrhea
counsel: Take with food and swallow the tablets whole at the same time each day
Check your blood sugar as instructed; report excessive thirst, frequent urination, confusion or breathing changes urgently
Stop the drug and seek care immediately for any spreading rash, blistering, mouth/eye sores, fever, or skin peeling
Report new or worsening cough or shortness of breath, and severe or persistent diarrhea
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed during treatment and for one week after the last dose
pk: Steady-state plasma concentrations reached within about 3 days of daily dosing
Median time to peak concentration (Tmax) about 2-4 hours under fed conditions
Once-daily dosing maintains exposure across the dosing interval
Store as labeled at controlled room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: Two key severe toxicities: severe hyperglycemia (including HHNKS/ketoacidosis) and severe cutaneous reactions (SJS, EM, TEN, DRESS)
Optimize blood glucose and check fasting glucose/HbA1c before starting and monitor throughout
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers and BCRP inhibitors
PIQRAY (breast cancer) is 300 mg/day with fulvestrant; VIJOICE (PROS) uses lower, age-based doses
Also causes pneumonitis and severe diarrhea/colitis; permanently discontinue for confirmed SCARs, severe hypersensitivity or pneumonitis
missed: For PIQRAY, a missed dose may be taken with food within 9 hours of the usual time; if more than 9 hours have passed, skip that day's dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited; reported effects are consistent with the known safety profile and include hyperglycemia, nausea, asthenia and rash. There is no known antidote. Initiate general symptomatic and supportive measures, including correction of hyperglycemia, as required.
